pages.text: Rice ripened yellow. Sparrows flocked down, chirping and pecking grains.
Dingding waved both hands. But birds avoided the clothesline, where cloth flapped.
Grandma took a tin can from the tool shed. "Hang this, and no birds come."
She hung it on a string. Wind made it clatter.
The birds flew up briefly, then landed again.
One sparrow sat on the can. Clatter, clatter. It did not budge.
Grandma hung another can. Now two birds sat there. "They have lost their fear."
Dingding took off the apron, tied it to a long pole, and planted it in the field's middle.
A gust made the apron flap. The birds fluttered away.
The field was quiet. A duck sat below the pole instead. Grandma quietly took down the cans.
